model.name: Application / Request Record
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to understand, create, inspect and operate a record of a request submitted by a party to a responsible body, from intent-to-submit through receipt, admissibility screening and handover into a case, service or fulfilment lifecycle.
model.scope_statement: The subject is the request-as-record: the identified, captured, evidentially reliable object created when a party asks a competent body to act (apply for authorisation, benefit, registration, court filing, information access, or a standard service request). Scope runs from the submission act to the disposition point at which a case is opened, the request is fulfilled, or the request is rejected/withdrawn/closed, plus the record's whole retention and disposal life. It covers identity, typing, parties and representation, declared content, evidence, completeness and validation, submission channel and receipt, integrity and non-repudiation, status and change, statutory clocks, routing, legal basis, fees, applicant rights, privacy, access, retention, exchange, provenance, measurement and exception handling. It deliberately excludes the substantive adjudication that follows.
in_scope: Identification, typing and classification of the request and its correlation identifiers across submitting, receiving and downstream systems
Applicant, beneficiary, representative and delegation roles, and the identity-assurance context of the submission act
Declared form content, attached and referenced evidence, and evidence retrieved from authoritative sources on the applicant's explicit request
Completeness/admissibility screening, technical validation and deficiency notification
Submission channel, receipt acknowledgement, and the distinct submission, receipt, registration and ingestion timestamps
Signature, seal, fixity and capture of the request as an authentic, reliable record
Request status model, amendment, supplementation, withdrawal and supersession
Statutory and service time limits, tolling, extension, tacit-approval and estimated completion dates
Routing to the competent body, processing track and priority, and handover into a case or fulfilment activity
Legal basis and collection authority, fees and payment conditionality
Applicant rights: reasons for rejection, redress routes, and data-subject rights over the request's personal data
Access control, confidentiality, retention, disposition and legal hold over the request record
Exchange packaging, standards alignment, provenance, performance measurement and exception handling
out_of_scope: Substantive adjudication, deliberation and the reasoning of the deciding body (WM-POL-017 Administrative case)
The decision, authorisation, permit, benefit award or refusal issued as the case output (separate outcome-record model)
Catalogue-level description of the public service itself: its requirements, channels, costs and outputs as published (CPSV-AP-aligned public-service model)
Master data for natural persons and organisations beyond the roles they play in this request (party/agent model)
Issuance, revocation and assurance-level certification of identity means and credentials (identity/trust-service model)
Payment execution, settlement, refund and accounting (payment model)
Content models and preservation of the evidence documents themselves beyond their reference, integrity and sufficiency (document/evidence record model)
Generic record semantics inherited from the parent record model (WM-REC-007)
Complaints, appeals and reviews against a decision, which are distinct triggering records
Incidents and unplanned service interruptions, which are a different trigger class from standard service requests
Case workload planning, resourcing and staff performance management

boundary_notes.distinction: This model specialises the generic record; it does not restate base record semantics. The record characteristics of authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability, and the general metadata/entity framework, are inherited rather than redefined here.

The application is the trigger and the durable evidence that a request was made; the case is the proceeding it opens. The boundary is the disposition event: once a case reference exists, case-internal steps, deliberation and outcome belong to WM-POL-017. A request may also close without ever opening a case.

CPSV-AP models the service, its Requirements, Evidence types, Channels, Costs, Rules and Outputs at catalogue level. This model instantiates them for one concrete request; it must not duplicate the catalogue definitions but must cite them.
Grant, refusal, authorisation or fulfilment result is a separate record with its own identity, effective dates and appeal window. This model holds only the reference and the disposition code.

A service request is a pre-defined, pre-approved ask for a standard service; an incident is an unplanned interruption or quality reduction. Standards treat them as separate resolution flows and they must not share one lifecycle model.

Attachments are referenced entities with their own identity, integrity and retention. This model records what evidence a requirement demands, whether it was supplied or fetched, and whether it was judged sufficient, not the document's internal content model.
Assurance levels, credential issuance and trust lists are governed elsewhere. This model records only the authentication context asserted at submission time and its evidential weight.

A right-of-access or erasure request is itself an instance of this model, but the controller's substantive compliance workflow and the rights framework belong to a privacy-governance model. Only the request-handling surface is modelled here.

sources.title: Core Public Service Vocabulary Application Profile (CPSV-AP) 3.2.0
sources.relevance: Normative EU application profile defining Public Service, Requirement, Evidence, Channel, Cost, Rule, Output, Participation, Agent and Event. Supplies the catalogue-side vocabulary that an individual request instantiates, and fixes the Evidence-proves-Requirement relation used for completeness screening.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2018/1724 establishing a single digital gateway
sources.organization: European Union (text as published by The National Archives, legislation.gov.uk)
sources.version_or_date: Regulation of 2 October 2018; consolidated text accessed 2026-08-24
sources.relevance: Article 6 (procedures to be offered fully online), Article 13 (cross-border access to online procedures) and Article 14 (technical system for cross-border automated exchange of evidence and the once-only principle, including explicit request and preview) ground the online-submission, evidence-sourcing and cross-border findings. Caveat: this is a national mirror of the EU act, not the OJ original.

sources.title: Directive 2006/123/EC on services in the internal market, Article 13 (Authorisation procedures)
sources.organization: European Union (text as published by The National Archives, legislation.gov.uk)
sources.version_or_date: Directive of 12 December 2006; Article 13 text accessed 2026-08-24
sources.relevance: The strongest normative source for application-handling duties: prompt acknowledgement of receipt stating the processing period, available means of redress and any tacit-authorisation effect; fixed and pre-published time limits with one justified extension; prompt notification of missing documents and of any effect on the clock; prompt reasoned rejection. Caveat: national mirror text.

sources.title: FHIR ServiceRequest resource, FHIR Release 5
sources.relevance: A mature, independently governed model of 'a record of a request for service': identifier assigned by orderer/receiver/fulfiller, status, intent (proposal|plan|directive|order), priority, category, code, subject, requester, performer, occurrence, authoredOn, supportingInfo. Validates separating request identity, intent and status, and separating requester from beneficiary.

sources.title: FHIR Task resource, FHIR Release 5
sources.relevance: Supplies an evidenced request-fulfilment state set (draft, requested, received, accepted, rejected, ready, cancelled, in-progress, on-hold, failed, completed, entered-in-error), the distinction between technical status and businessStatus, statusReason, restriction, input and output. Directly grounds the status model and the entered-in-error correction path.

sources.title: Electronic Court Filing Version 5.0, Committee Specification 01
sources.organization: OASIS LegalXML Electronic Court Filing TC
sources.relevance: A concrete, normative submission-intake specification: FilingMessage with lead and connected documents, ReviewFiling then accepted/rejected clerk review, RecordDocketing and NotifyDocketingComplete, a persistent filing tracking identifier usable for status query after docketing, filer and participant roles, and optional payment messages. Grounds receipt, review, routing and handover findings.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Entity/Activity/Agent with wasGeneratedBy, wasDerivedFrom, wasAttributedTo, wasAssociatedWith, actedOnBehalfOf, startedAtTime, endedAtTime and the qualified pattern (Generation, Derivation, Delegation, Bundle). Grounds chain-of-custody, representation-as-delegation and supersession-as-derivation without inventing bespoke provenance vocabulary.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Mandates a full date-time with seconds and an explicit UTC offset ('Z' or +hh:mm), giving a sortable, unambiguous timestamp form. Normative basis for the model's timestamp rule and for distinguishing submission, receipt, registration and ingestion instants across time zones.

sources.title: RFC 9562: Universally Unique IDentifiers (UUIDs)
sources.relevance: Defines UUIDv4 and the time-ordered UUIDv7, states that global uniqueness cannot be guaranteed without a shared scheme, and cautions against name-based identifiers as primary keys in favour of time-based surrogate keys. Supports the third tier of the identity priority rule.

sources.title: Guidelines 01/2022 on data subject rights - Right of access, Version 2.1
sources.relevance: Authoritative interpretation that a request needs no particular form or channel, that requester identification must be proportionate and not a barrier, and that the one-month deadline runs from receipt with a conditional two-month extension. Grounds the channel-neutrality, identification-proportionality and clock findings for rights-based requests.

sources.title: Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR) Article 12 as assimilated in UK law
sources.version_or_date: Assimilated text accessed 2026-08-24, reflecting UK amendments in force
sources.relevance: Transparency and request-handling modalities: response without undue delay, electronic reply when the request was electronic, reasonable fee or refusal only for manifestly unfounded or excessive requests with the burden on the controller, and additional identifying information where identity is reasonably doubted. Recorded as a UK-divergent variant, not as the EU text.

sources.title: 5 U.S. Code § 552 - Public information; agency rules, opinions, orders, records, and proceedings
sources.organization: Cornell Law School Legal Information Institute (publishing the United States Code)
sources.relevance: A counterexample jurisdiction with explicit intake mechanics: 20-working-day determination running from receipt by the proper component (no later than ten days after initial receipt), tolling only to seek clarification or resolve fees, a ten-working-day unusual-circumstances extension with expected completion date, expedited processing decided within ten days, and a statutory duty to assign an individualised tracking number for requests taking longer than ten days plus status and estimated completion date. Used as secondary because LII republishes rather than promulgates.

sources.title: ISO 23081-2:2021 Information and documentation - Metadata for managing records - Part 2: Conceptual and implementation issues
sources.relevance: Framework for records metadata built on the record / agent / business / mandate / relationship entity view, aimed at standardised description of records and their contextual entities, fixed points of aggregation for interoperability, and reuse of metadata over time and across applications. Grounds the separation of request metadata from party, mandate and process metadata. Caveat: normative text is paywalled; only the public abstract and scope were read.

sources.title: ISO 15489-1:2016 Information and documentation - Records management - Part 1: Concepts and principles
sources.relevance: Establishes that records are authoritative evidence of business only while they retain authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability, and frames appraisal, records controls and the create/capture/control processes. Grounds capture, fixity, disposition-authority and usability requirements. Caveat: the ISO catalogue page returned HTTP 403 to automated retrieval and the normative text is paywalled; only the widely republished characteristic set and scope are relied on.

sources.title: MoReq2010 Modular Requirements for Records Systems
sources.version_or_date: MoReq2010 v1.1, launched May 2011; site accessed 2026-08-24
sources.relevance: Service-based records-system specification in which every entity carries metadata, an event history and an access control list, records sit in aggregations, and retention rules are inherited from a classification. Grounds the event-history, access-control-list and disposition-scheduling findings as system-independent requirements rather than product features.

sources.title: NIEMOpen - National Information Exchange Model
sources.organization: OASIS Open Project (NIEMOpen); sponsors include DHS S&T and FBI CJIS
sources.relevance: A governed common vocabulary with domain content, Message Exchange Packages, Naming and Design Rules and multiple serialisations (XML, JSON). Evidence that exchange packaging and naming rules are a distinct concern from the semantic record, supporting the format-neutrality principle.

sources.title: Verifiable Credentials Data Model v2.0
sources.relevance: issuer, credentialSubject, validFrom/validUntil, credentialStatus, credentialSchema, evidence and proof, plus verifiable presentations supporting selective disclosure. Grounds evidence provenance, validity windows, revocation checking at the time of reliance, and data-minimising evidence attachment.

sources.title: Case Management Model and Notation (CMMN) Version 1.1
sources.relevance: A common meta-model and notation for modelling a Case and exchanging Case models. Defines the neighbouring concept precisely enough to fix the boundary between the triggering request record and the case it opens, and shows that case content is modelled separately from the intake artefact.

sources.title: GOV.UK Service Manual - Service Standard
sources.relevance: Public-authority requirements that shape request intake: solve a whole problem, provide a joined-up experience across all channels, make sure everyone can use the service, protect users' privacy, define what success looks like and publish performance data, and use open standards and common patterns. Grounds the channel-equity and performance-measurement findings.

bundles.name: Request Identity, Typing and Actors
bundles.description: Establishes what a single request is, how it is named and classified, and which parties stand behind it and with what identity assurance.
bundles.rationale: Every downstream operation - deduplication, routing, clock computation, access control, disposal - depends on a stable answer to 'which request is this and whose is it'. Independently governed request models all begin with an identifier, a type/code and a requester distinct from the subject, so this concern is separated first.

layers.name: Identity and Classification
layers.description: Identifiers, naming authority, correlation across systems, and the typing/classification that determines which rules apply.

findings.name: Request identifier set and naming authority
findings.description: A request typically carries several identifiers at once: one assigned by the submitter, one assigned by the receiving body at registration, and internal surrogate keys. Which one is authoritative, when each is minted, and how they correlate must be explicit.

questions.text: Which identifier is the authoritative public reference for this request, which body minted it, and at which lifecycle event was it minted?
Which additional identifiers exist for the same request, and what is the declared equivalence relation between them?
answer_data: Identifier collection with scheme, issuer and role

questions.text: Is a tracking reference disclosed to the requester, and by when is disclosure required?
answer_data: Disclosure obligation flag and trigger condition

questions.text: How are duplicate submissions of the same underlying request detected and reconciled without destroying either record?

data_elements.name: Authoritative request identifier
data_elements.description: The identifier assigned by the master system of record for this request, used as the public reference.

data_elements.name: Alternate identifiers
data_elements.description: Submitter reference, channel transaction id, internal surrogate key and any partner-system identifiers, each with scheme and issuer.

data_elements.name: Duplicate-of reference
data_elements.description: Link to a prior request judged to be the same underlying ask.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Identifiers are inline scalar values on the request record and pointers into externally governed identifier schemes. No separate stored artefact exists; producing one would create a second place where identity could drift from the master system.

findings.name: Request type, procedure binding and classification
findings.description: The request must be bound to the specific procedure or service being requested, because the applicable evidence requirements, time limits, fees and competent authority all derive from that binding rather than from the request itself.

questions.text: Which published service or procedure, at which version, does this request instantiate?
What request intent does this record express - a proposal, a plan, or an actionable order to the receiving body?
Which classification schemes are applied to the request, and which of them are normative for processing rather than merely descriptive?
If the catalogue definition changes after submission, does the request remain governed by the version in force at submission?
answer_data: Catalogue version in force at submission

data_elements.name: Procedure or service reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the catalogue entry describing the requested service, including its version.

data_elements.name: Request intent
data_elements.description: Degree of actionability the requester attaches to the request.

data_elements.name: Request category codes
data_elements.description: Coded classifications applied for routing, statistics or legal treatment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Typing is a set of coded references into externally maintained catalogues and code lists. The catalogue entry itself is an artefact of the sibling public-service model; duplicating it here would fork the authoritative definition.

layers.name: Parties, Representation and Identity Assurance
layers.description: Who submits, who benefits, who is authorised to act for whom, and how strongly the submitter was identified.

findings.name: Parties, roles and authority to act
findings.description: The submitter, the beneficiary and the legally responsible party are frequently different, and third-party submission requires an evidenced mandate. Conflating them produces wrong notifications, wrong appeal rights and wrong privacy treatment.

questions.text: Who is the beneficiary or subject of the request, and is that party distinct from the submitter?
Where a representative acts, what is the evidenced basis and scope of that mandate, and when does it expire?
answer_data: Mandate validity period start and end

questions.text: Which party carries legal responsibility for the truth of the declarations, and which party receives official notifications?
answer_data: Notification address or channel per party

questions.text: How are role changes during processing - change of representative, death, insolvency, transfer of the underlying interest - recorded without rewriting history?
answer_data: Change event record with reason code

data_elements.name: Party role assignment
data_elements.description: A time-bounded association of a party to the request in a named role (submitter, subject, representative, payer, notified party).

data_elements.name: Mandate or power-of-attorney reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the evidence authorising a representative to act, with scope and validity window.

data_elements.name: Notification target
data_elements.description: The address or channel to which official communications about this request must be sent.

artifacts.name: Mandate / authority-to-act evidence
artifacts.description: The document or credential establishing that a representative may submit and act on the request, together with its scope and validity window.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the issuing registry's mandate identifier where one exists; otherwise the credential identifier; otherwise a UUID assigned at capture, always paired with the issuer reference and validity period.

findings.name: Identity assurance context of the submission act
findings.description: The evidential weight of a request depends on how the submitter was identified at the moment of submission. Assurance must be recorded as an observed fact about that act, not inferred later from the account that holds the record.

questions.text: By what means was the submitter authenticated at submission, and at what assurance level?
Which asserted attributes were verified against an authoritative source, and which remain self-declared?
If identity could not be established to the required level, what proportionate additional identification was requested, and did the clock stop?
Is anonymous or pseudonymous submission permitted for this procedure, and what limits does that place on the outcome?

data_elements.name: Authentication context
data_elements.description: Method, provider, assurance level and timestamp of the authentication that accompanied the submission act.

data_elements.name: Attribute verification status
data_elements.description: Per-attribute record of whether a declared value was verified, by whom and when.

artifacts.name: Authentication / identity assertion record
artifacts.description: The retained assertion evidencing how the submitter was identified at submission time, sufficient to reconstruct assurance later without re-contacting the identity provider.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Use the assertion identifier issued by the identity provider; where absent, a UUID assigned at capture bound to the request identifier and the RFC 3339 authentication instant.

bundles.name: Declared Content, Evidence and Validation
bundles.description: What the requester actually asserted, what proof was attached or fetched, and whether the package is technically valid and legally admissible.
bundles.rationale: Application profiles model Evidence as proof that a Requirement is met, and intake specifications separate technical conformance from substantive review. Keeping declared content, evidence sufficiency and validation distinct prevents a schema error from being mistaken for an inadmissible application.

layers.name: Declared Content and Evidence
layers.description: The form instance, its attachments, and evidence obtained from authoritative sources instead of the applicant.

findings.name: Form definition, instance and declarations
findings.description: A request instantiates a versioned form or payload definition. The definition and the instance are separate objects with separate lifecycles, and the definition in force at submission must remain retrievable for as long as the instance is kept.

questions.text: Which form or payload definition, at which version, does this instance conform to, and is that definition still retrievable?
Which declarations, attestations or consents did the requester make, and what is the legal effect of each?
In which language was the request submitted, and does the procedure require translation or a specific official language?
Which declared values are free text and which are bound to controlled vocabularies, and how are unbound values handled downstream?
answer_data: Code system reference per bound field

data_elements.name: Form definition reference
data_elements.description: Versioned pointer to the definition the submitted payload conforms to.

data_elements.name: Declared payload
data_elements.description: The structured set of values asserted by the requester, independent of any serialisation.

data_elements.name: Declaration acceptance
data_elements.description: Record of each attestation or consent accepted, with timestamp.

data_elements.name: Submission language
data_elements.description: Language in which the request was made.

artifacts.name: Submitted request payload as filed
artifacts.description: The immutable as-filed content of the request, retained separately from any later working copy so that what was actually submitted can always be reproduced.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the authoritative request identifier plus a version ordinal; each amendment produces a new immutable instance rather than mutating the prior one.

findings.name: Evidence requirements, attachments and sufficiency
findings.description: Evidence is proof that a stated requirement is met. The model must record which requirement each item of evidence discharges, not merely that files were attached, otherwise sufficiency cannot be assessed or re-assessed.

questions.text: Which requirement does each supplied evidence item discharge, and are any mandatory requirements still undischarged?
Is an evidence item still valid at the moment of reliance, and was its status checked then?
How is each attachment's integrity established and preserved between submission and reliance?
Where alternative evidence is acceptable, which alternative was chosen and who accepted the substitution?

data_elements.name: Evidence item
data_elements.description: A supplied or referenced proof, with type, source, format, digest and validity window.

data_elements.name: Requirement discharge link
data_elements.description: Association between a catalogue requirement and the evidence judged to satisfy it, with status.

data_elements.name: Evidence content digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest of the attachment as received, with named algorithm.

artifacts.name: Evidence manifest
artifacts.description: An enumeration of every evidence item bound to the request, the requirement each discharges, its origin, its digest and its validity, forming the sufficiency baseline.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Derived identity: request identifier plus manifest version ordinal; regenerated as a new version whenever evidence is added, replaced or withdrawn.

findings.name: Evidence obtained from authoritative sources on explicit request
findings.description: Where a body may fetch evidence from another authority rather than ask the applicant, the model must record the applicant's explicit request, any preview and rejection of the fetched evidence, and the provenance of the retrieved item.

questions.text: Did the requester explicitly request that evidence be fetched from another authority, and how is that explicit request evidenced?
Was the retrieved evidence previewed by the requester before use, and could it be rejected?
answer_data: Preview outcome code (used, rejected, not exercised)

questions.text: Which authority provided the evidence, under which mapping between the requirement and that authority's evidence type?
What happens to the request when authoritative retrieval fails or returns no match?
answer_data: Fallback path code (applicant supplies, manual channel, refusal)

data_elements.name: Explicit request record
data_elements.description: Evidence that the requester asked for cross-authority evidence retrieval, with scope and timestamp.

data_elements.name: Evidence retrieval activity
data_elements.description: Provenance record of a retrieval: requesting body, providing body, start and end instants, outcome.

data_elements.name: Preview outcome
data_elements.description: Whether the requester previewed retrieved evidence and whether it was used or rejected.

artifacts.name: Explicit request and preview record
artifacts.description: The retained record of the applicant's explicit authorisation for cross-authority evidence retrieval and of any preview exercised, kept because it is the lawful basis for the retrieval.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus retrieval activity identifier; where the exchange system issues its own correlation identifier, that value takes precedence as the authoritative key.

layers.name: Completeness, Admissibility and Technical Validation
layers.description: Two separate gates: does the package parse and conform, and is the request legally admissible and complete enough to start.

findings.name: Completeness screening and admissibility determination
findings.description: A request that is received is not necessarily perfected. Bodies commonly owe a duty to notify missing documents promptly and to say whether the processing clock is affected, and admissibility is a reviewable determination in its own right.

questions.text: Against which criteria is completeness assessed, and who is competent to make that determination?
When a deficiency is found, what must the notice tell the requester and by when must it be sent?
What effect does a deficiency have on the statutory clock - suspension, restart, or none - and on what legal basis?
If the requester does not cure the deficiency, what disposition follows and is it appealable?
Is completeness screening re-run after amendment, and does an amended request inherit the original submission date?

data_elements.name: Completeness determination
data_elements.description: Outcome, agent, basis and timestamp of the assessment that the request is or is not complete.

data_elements.name: Deficiency item
data_elements.description: A specific missing or defective element, with the requirement it relates to and the cure deadline.

data_elements.name: Effective submission instant
data_elements.description: The instant from which the procedure is legally treated as started, which may differ from first receipt.

artifacts.name: Deficiency / further-information notice
artifacts.description: The outbound notice telling the requester what is missing, by when it must be supplied, and what effect the deficiency has on the processing period.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus a monotonically increasing notice sequence number within the request; where a correspondence register exists, its register identifier is authoritative.

findings.name: Technical validation, business rules and error reporting
findings.description: Conformance checking against schema, code lists and business rules is distinct from legal admissibility and must produce machine-actionable, citable errors bound to specific fields.

questions.text: Which validation layers apply - structural, code-list, cross-field, cross-record - and in which order are they executed?
answer_data: Blocking versus advisory marker per layer

questions.text: How is each validation failure identified so a requester or agent can locate and fix it?
Which rules are enforced at submission time versus after receipt, and what is the consequence of that placement?
When a rule set changes, are previously accepted requests revalidated, and how is a legacy pass recorded?

data_elements.name: Validation outcome
data_elements.description: Aggregate pass/fail result of a validation run, with rule set version and timestamp.

data_elements.name: Validation issue
data_elements.description: A single detected problem with code, location, severity and message.

artifacts.name: Validation report
artifacts.description: The retained result of a validation run over the submitted package, enumerating issues with codes and locations, retained as evidence of why a submission was or was not accepted technically.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus validation run ordinal and RFC 3339 run instant; each re-run creates a new report rather than overwriting.

bundles.name: Submission Act, Channel and Record Capture
bundles.description: The act of submitting, the channel used, the receipt owed to the requester, and the capture of the submission as an authentic record.
bundles.rationale: Records become authoritative evidence only if captured with authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability preserved; and authorisation procedures impose an explicit duty to acknowledge receipt. The submission act is therefore a first-class, separately governed concern rather than a side effect of data entry.

layers.name: Submission, Receipt and Channel
layers.description: The instants that matter, the acknowledgement owed, and the channel through which the request arrived.

findings.name: Submission, receipt, registration and ingestion instants
findings.description: Four distinct instants routinely diverge: when the requester submitted, when the body received it, when the proper component received it, and when the system ingested it. Legal effects attach to different ones, so they must be recorded separately with explicit offsets.

questions.text: Which instants are captured for this request and which one starts the legally relevant period?
Which clock and time zone are authoritative when the requester and the receiving body are in different zones, and how are out-of-hours and deadline-day submissions treated?
What must the acknowledgement of receipt tell the requester, and within what period must it be issued?
answer_data: Issue deadline and actual issue instant

questions.text: How is receipt proven if the acknowledgement is never delivered or is disputed?

data_elements.name: Submission instant
data_elements.description: When the requester completed the submission act, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with seconds and explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Receipt instant
data_elements.description: When the receiving body took possession of the request; may differ from the submission instant.

data_elements.name: Registration instant
data_elements.description: When the request was formally entered on the register and given its authoritative identifier.

data_elements.name: Ingestion instant
data_elements.description: When the record was captured into the managing system, recorded separately from the event instants.

artifacts.name: Acknowledgement of receipt
artifacts.description: The receipt issued to the requester stating the processing period, redress routes, any tacit-approval effect and the tracking reference; it is the requester's primary proof that the request exists.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Carries the authoritative request identifier as its subject key and its own receipt serial from the issuing register; the pair is the citable reference.

findings.name: Channel, cross-border access and accessibility equity
findings.description: The channel is not a delivery detail: it determines available evidence-fetching, identity assurance, accessibility obligations and, for cross-border requesters, whether the procedure is usable at all. Outcomes must not depend on the channel chosen.

questions.text: Through which channel was the request submitted, and which channels are formally equivalent for this procedure?
Can a non-resident or cross-border requester complete this procedure through the same channel with a foreign identity means?
What accessibility and assisted-route provision exists for requesters who cannot use the primary channel?
Does the channel affect the legal treatment of the request - fees, deadlines, evidence, or the reply format owed?

data_elements.name: Submission channel
data_elements.description: The medium through which the request reached the body, referencing the catalogue channel definition.

data_elements.name: Reasonable adjustment record
data_elements.description: Any accommodation applied so the requester could submit or be served.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The channel is a coded reference into the sibling public-service catalogue, which owns the Channel object with its availability, cost and constraints. Holding a copy here would create a second, drifting definition of the same channel; only the reference and any request-specific adjustment are inline.

layers.name: Authenticity, Integrity and Capture
layers.description: Signature, seal, fixity and the act of capturing the request into a managed records system.

findings.name: Capture, fixity, signature and non-repudiation
findings.description: To function as authoritative evidence the request must be captured so that it is what it purports to be, complete and unaltered, and retrievable and interpretable for as long as it is needed. Signatures and seals support attribution; fixity supports integrity; neither substitutes for the other.

questions.text: What binds the request content to its submitter in a way that resists later repudiation?
answer_data: Signature validation result and validation instant

questions.text: How is integrity of the as-captured record demonstrated at any later date?
answer_data: Fixity re-check schedule and last result

questions.text: At what point is the request formally captured as a record, and what becomes immutable at that point?
How will the record remain interpretable if its original format or signature algorithm becomes obsolete?

data_elements.name: Fixity digest
data_elements.description: Digest of the as-captured request package with named algorithm and computation instant.

data_elements.name: Signature validation result
data_elements.description: Outcome of validating a signature or seal, with the instant of validation and the trust anchor used.

data_elements.name: Capture event
data_elements.description: The event that brought the request under records control, with capturing system and instant.

artifacts.name: Sealed submission package
artifacts.description: The bundled as-received request with its attachments, signatures, seals, transport metadata and fixity values, retained as the evidential original.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Authoritative request identifier plus package digest; the digest is the tamper-evident secondary key and must be recorded at capture, not recomputed on demand.

bundles.name: Status, Change, Time and Handover
bundles.description: How the request moves through states, how it may lawfully change, how its clocks are computed, and how it hands over to a case or fulfilment.
bundles.rationale: Independently governed request models converge on an explicit status set with reasons and a separate business status, and authorisation law imposes fixed pre-published periods with defined extension and tacit-approval effects. These are the operating mechanics an agent must get right.

layers.name: Status Model and Permitted Change
layers.description: The state set and transitions, and the amendment, withdrawal and supersession paths.

findings.name: Status set, transitions and status reasons
findings.description: A defensible status model distinguishes the technical processing state from the business-meaningful state, records a reason for every non-obvious state, and keeps an explicit erroneous-entry state separate from legitimate cancellation.

questions.text: What is the complete set of states this request can occupy, and which are terminal?
Which state transitions are permitted, who may trigger each, and what precondition must hold?
answer_data: Transition list with source and target state

questions.text: How is the technical processing state distinguished from the business status the requester is told about?
How is a request recorded that should never have existed, as distinct from one properly cancelled or withdrawn?

data_elements.name: Request status
data_elements.description: Current processing state of the request from the governed state set.

data_elements.name: Status reason
data_elements.description: Coded and free-text explanation of why the request is in its current state.

data_elements.name: Business status
data_elements.description: Workflow-meaningful status communicated to the requester, distinct from the technical state.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Current status is a single inline coded value; its history is not stored here but in the event-history artefact defined under the temporal layer. Materialising a second status artefact would create two competing sources of truth for the same state.

findings.name: Amendment, supplementation, withdrawal and supersession
findings.description: Requests change after submission. Each change class has different legal consequences for the submission date, the clock and the evidence baseline, and none may erase the prior state.

questions.text: Which change classes are permitted after submission, and until which point in the lifecycle?
answer_data: Cut-off state or instant per class

questions.text: Does an amendment create a new version of the same request or a new request that supersedes the old one?
What effect does each change class have on the effective submission date and the running deadline?
On withdrawal, what is retained, what is returned, and what is the requester told?

data_elements.name: Version ordinal
data_elements.description: Monotonic version number of the request content, incremented on each accepted amendment.

data_elements.name: Supersession link
data_elements.description: Derivation relation to the request or version this one replaces.

data_elements.name: Change event
data_elements.description: Record of an amendment, supplementation or withdrawal with class, actor, reason and instant.

artifacts.name: Amendment / withdrawal notice
artifacts.description: The instrument by which the requester or body records a change or withdrawal, retained because it evidences consent to alter or end the request.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus change sequence number; where a correspondence register exists its identifier is authoritative, and the notice always cites the version ordinal it acts on.

layers.name: Time Limits and Event History
layers.description: Statutory and service clocks, their suspension and extension, and the append-only history of what happened when.

findings.name: Processing periods, tolling, extension and tacit outcomes
findings.description: Processing periods must be fixed and published in advance, are commonly extendable once on justified grounds with notice before expiry, may be tolled in defined circumstances, and in some regimes expiry produces a deemed grant. Clock state is derived data that must be reproducible from recorded events.

questions.text: What processing period applies, on what legal basis, and where was it published in advance?
answer_data: Calendar basis (working days versus calendar days)

questions.text: From which recorded instant does the period run, and how is that instant chosen when receipt is staged across components?
Under which conditions may the clock be suspended or extended, who authorises it, and what notice is owed before expiry?
What happens on expiry - deemed grant, deemed refusal, or continued duty to decide - and how is that outcome recorded?
Is an estimated completion date communicated to the requester, and how is it revised?

data_elements.name: Processing deadline
data_elements.description: The computed instant by which the body must respond, derived from the clock-start instant and the applicable period.

data_elements.name: Clock suspension interval
data_elements.description: A tolling interval with start, end, reason and authorising basis.

data_elements.name: Extension grant
data_elements.description: A recorded extension with justification, granting actor, new deadline and notice instant.

data_elements.name: Tacit outcome indicator
data_elements.description: Whether silence on expiry produces a deemed grant, deemed refusal, or no automatic effect.

artifacts.name: Time-limit and extension notification
artifacts.description: Outbound notices stating the applicable period, any extension with its justification, and the estimated completion date, retained as evidence that the notice duty was met before expiry.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus notice sequence number and RFC 3339 dispatch instant; the dispatch instant, not the drafting instant, is the evidential value.

findings.name: Append-only event history and audit trail
findings.description: Every entity in a defensible records system carries an event history. For a request this history is both the operational timeline and the audit evidence, and it must distinguish when something happened from when it was recorded.

questions.text: Which event types must be recorded for a request, and is the history append-only?
For each event, is the event instant recorded separately from the observation or ingestion instant?
Which agent, human or software, is attributed to each event, and on whose behalf did it act?
How long is the event history retained relative to the request content, and can it be disposed of separately?
answer_data: Rationale for divergence from content retention

data_elements.name: Event history entry
data_elements.description: One immutable entry: event type, event instant, recording instant, acting agent, affected element and outcome.

data_elements.name: Event instant
data_elements.description: When the event actually occurred, as an RFC 3339 timestamp with explicit offset.

data_elements.name: Recording instant
data_elements.description: When the event was observed and written to the history, distinct from the event instant.

artifacts.name: Request event history
artifacts.description: The append-only sequence of events for the request, functioning as its audit trail and as the derivation source for every computed clock or status value.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound one-to-one to the authoritative request identifier; individual entries keyed by a monotonic sequence number plus event instant, never by timestamp alone since timestamps can collide.

layers.name: Routing, Prioritisation and Handover
layers.description: Determining the competent body and processing track, and the disposition that ends the request's own lifecycle.

findings.name: Competent body determination, transfer and processing track
findings.description: A request may arrive at the wrong body or the wrong component. Competence determination, onward transfer with a preserved receipt date, and assignment to a processing track are distinct operations each with their own evidence and timing consequences.

questions.text: Which body is competent for this request, on what jurisdictional or subject-matter basis, and who determined that?
When a request is transferred, what date does the receiving body treat as receipt, and is the requester notified?
Into which processing track is the request placed, on what criteria, and can the requester request expedition?
How is priority or queue position made auditable so that ordering can be shown to be non-arbitrary?

data_elements.name: Competent body assignment
data_elements.description: The body currently responsible, with basis and effective period.

data_elements.name: Processing track
data_elements.description: The queue or track into which the request is placed for handling.

data_elements.name: Expedition determination
data_elements.description: Outcome, reason and instant of a decision on expedited handling.

artifacts.name: Transfer / referral notice
artifacts.description: The record of forwarding a request to another body or component, preserving the original receipt date and evidencing that the requester was told where the request went.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus transfer sequence number; the notice must carry both the originating and receiving body identifiers and the original receipt instant.

findings.name: Case opening, fulfilment and final disposition of the request
findings.description: The request's own lifecycle ends at disposition: a case is opened, the service is fulfilled directly, or the request is refused, withdrawn or closed. This is the boundary handover to the neighbouring case model and must be an explicit, linked event.

questions.text: What disposition ended the request's own lifecycle, and when?
If a case or proceeding was opened, what is its identifier and what is the typed relation between request and case?
Can one request open several cases, or several requests be consolidated into one case, and how is that recorded?
Where the request is refused at intake, what reasons must be given and which redress route is stated?
After disposition, does the request record remain independently addressable and queryable for status?
answer_data: Redirection rule to the case record

data_elements.name: Disposition code
data_elements.description: How the request lifecycle ended: case opened, fulfilled, refused, withdrawn, closed, entered in error.

data_elements.name: Case reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the case or proceeding opened as a result of the request.

data_elements.name: Outcome reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the decision or output record produced, held in the sibling outcome model.

artifacts.name: Case-opening or intake-refusal notice
artifacts.description: The instrument recording that a case was opened with its reference, or that the request was refused at intake with reasons and redress information.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus the newly minted case identifier where a case exists; for refusals, request identifier plus notice sequence number.

bundles.name: Legal Basis, Rights, Privacy and Stewardship
bundles.description: Why the body may collect this request at all, what it may charge, what the requester is owed, and how the record is protected, restricted and eventually disposed of.
bundles.rationale: Collection authority, applicant rights and disposition are legally mandated dimensions that intake systems routinely under-model. Authorisation-procedure law fixes the rights side, records standards fix the disposition side, and privacy authorities fix the personal-data side.

layers.name: Collection Authority and Cost
layers.description: The mandate to require this information and the fees attached to the request.

findings.name: Legal basis, mandate and authority to collect
findings.description: A request form is a collection of information exercised under a mandate. The mandate, the burden imposed and any approval or reference required for the collection are context an agent must be able to cite, not assume.

questions.text: Under which instrument is the body empowered to require this request and this information, and is that instrument cited to the requester?
Is the request voluntary or mandatory, and what follows from not providing a given item?
answer_data: Voluntary or mandatory marker per item

questions.text: Is a collection approval, control number or equivalent registration required before the form may be used, and is it current?
What burden does the request impose on the requester, and is that estimate published?

data_elements.name: Legal basis reference
data_elements.description: The instrument authorising the procedure and the collection of the requested information.

data_elements.name: Collection approval reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and expiry of any required approval or registration for the information collection.

data_elements.name: Mandatory-provision marker
data_elements.description: Per data item, whether provision is mandatory and what the consequence of omission is.

artifacts.name: Collection authority and burden statement
artifacts.description: The statement presented with the form giving the legal authority for the collection, whether provision is mandatory, the consequences of non-provision and any burden estimate or approval reference.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by the form definition identifier and version rather than by request, since the statement is a property of the collection instrument; each request records which version it was shown.

findings.name: Fees, waivers and payment as an admissibility condition
findings.description: Charges attach to many requests and unresolved fee questions can lawfully stop the clock or block admissibility. The model records the fee position and its effect on processing, not the payment transaction itself.

questions.text: What charge applies to this request, on what basis, and does it vary by channel or requester category?
Is payment a precondition of admissibility, and what is the effect of non-payment on the clock and the disposition?
On what grounds may a fee be waived, reduced or refunded, and who decides?
When may a charge be refused as excessive, or a request refused as manifestly unfounded, and who bears the burden of showing that?

data_elements.name: Fee assessment
data_elements.description: Assessed charge with basis, amount, currency and calculation instant.

data_elements.name: Fee status
data_elements.description: Whether the charge is outstanding, paid, waived, reduced or refunded, with the effect on admissibility.

data_elements.name: Payment reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the payment transaction held in the sibling payment model.

artifacts.name: Fee assessment and waiver determination
artifacts.description: The record of the charge calculated for the request, any waiver or reduction granted with reasons, and the resulting effect on admissibility and the clock.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus assessment sequence number; recalculation produces a new assessment rather than editing the prior one, so the basis at each point remains reconstructible.

layers.name: Applicant Rights and Personal Data
layers.description: What the requester is entitled to receive and challenge, and how personal data in the request is lawfully handled.

findings.name: Reasons, notification and routes of redress
findings.description: Requesters are owed prompt reasoned communication of adverse determinations and a statement of the means of redress available, with the redress clock typically running from that notification.

questions.text: Which determinations trigger a duty to give reasons, and to what standard of specificity?
Which redress routes are available, with what deadlines, and were they stated to the requester in writing?
Is the requester entitled to be heard or to correct the record before an adverse determination is made?
How is the notification instant established for the purpose of starting the redress clock?

data_elements.name: Adverse determination record
data_elements.description: A determination against the requester with its reasons, legal basis, agent and instant.

data_elements.name: Redress route
data_elements.description: Available challenge mechanism with forum, deadline and any precondition.

artifacts.name: Reasoned determination and redress notice
artifacts.description: The written communication giving the determination, its reasons and legal basis, and the available means of redress with deadlines; it is the instrument the redress clock runs from.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus determination sequence number, with the RFC 3339 dispatch instant recorded as the legally operative value alongside any deemed-receipt date.

findings.name: Personal data categories and lawful processing context
findings.description: Requests concentrate personal data, often including special categories, supplied by a person exercising a right. The processing basis, minimisation position and controller/processor roles must be recorded against the request, not only at system level.

questions.text: Which categories of personal data does this request contain, and are any of them special-category or otherwise heightened-risk?
answer_data: Location of each category in the payload or attachments

questions.text: What is the lawful basis for processing each category, and does that basis persist after disposition?
Which body is controller and which are processors or joint controllers for this request, including exchange intermediaries?
What minimisation was applied - which requested items were reduced, redacted or not collected - and on what assessment?
Can the requester exercise data-subject rights over this request record, and how does that interact with the procedure's own retention duty?

data_elements.name: Personal data category
data_elements.description: A category of personal data present in the request, with sensitivity classification and location.

data_elements.name: Lawful processing basis
data_elements.description: The basis relied on for processing, per category, with reference and effective period.

data_elements.name: Controller and processor roles
data_elements.description: Which entity controls and which process the request's personal data, with effective periods.

artifacts.name: Processing record entry for the request category
artifacts.description: The register entry describing purposes, categories, recipients, transfers and retention for requests of this type, which the individual request instance references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by procedure identifier and register entry version rather than by individual request; each request cites the entry version applicable at its submission instant.

layers.name: Access Control and Disposition
layers.description: Who may see the request and its parts, and when and how it is destroyed, transferred or preserved.

findings.name: Access control, confidentiality and public disclosure
findings.description: Every managed entity carries an access control list, and request records frequently mix a publicly disclosable shell with confidential content. Access must be expressible at element granularity and must survive export.

questions.text: Who may read, amend and dispose of this request, and at what granularity is that expressed?
answer_data: Permission entries by role or agent

questions.text: Which parts of the request are publicly disclosable and which are withheld, on what stated ground?
How does the requester's own access to their request differ from third-party or public access?
Do access markings and controls travel with the record when it is exported or transferred to another body?
answer_data: Markings carried in the export package

data_elements.name: Access control entry
data_elements.description: A grant of a named permission to a role or agent over a defined scope, with basis and validity period.

data_elements.name: Disclosability marking
data_elements.description: Per-element indication of whether content may be disclosed publicly and on what ground it is withheld.

artifacts.name: Access control list and redaction schedule
artifacts.description: The authoritative statement of who may do what to the request and which elements are redacted for which audience, retained so that historical access decisions remain reconstructible.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Bound to the request identifier with a version ordinal; each change appends a new version and the superseded version is retained for audit rather than overwritten.

findings.name: Retention rule, disposition action and legal hold
findings.description: Retention derives from a classification and a disposition authority, not from an ad hoc setting. Requests that never became cases, withdrawn requests and erroneous entries often carry different rules from the case file they would have joined.

questions.text: Which retention rule applies to this request, from which classification and under which disposition authority?
What event starts the retention period, and how is that trigger detected reliably?
Do withdrawn, refused-at-intake and entered-in-error requests follow the same rule as accepted ones?
What disposal actions are permitted, and what evidence of disposal is kept after the content is gone?
answer_data: Disposal action code (destroy, transfer, permanent retention, review)

questions.text: How is a legal hold applied and released, and what does it override?

data_elements.name: Retention rule binding
data_elements.description: The retention rule inherited from classification, with its version and the disposition authority behind it.

data_elements.name: Disposal-due instant
data_elements.description: Computed instant at which the disposal action becomes due, derived from the trigger and the retention period.

data_elements.name: Legal hold
data_elements.description: An active hold suspending disposal, with scope, applying authority and validity period.

data_elements.name: Disposal action record
data_elements.description: The executed disposal with action code, executor, instant and residual metadata retained.

artifacts.name: Disposition authority binding and disposal certificate
artifacts.description: The record binding the request to its retention rule and disposition authority, and, once executed, the certificate evidencing what was destroyed or transferred, by whom and when.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Disposition authority identifier plus request identifier for the binding; the certificate carries its own register serial from the disposal register, which survives destruction of the content.

bundles.name: Exchange, Provenance, Measurement and Exceptions
bundles.description: How the request moves between systems, how its history is attributable, how the intake service is measured, and what happens when things go wrong.
bundles.rationale: Exchange packaging and naming rules are a distinct governed layer from the semantic record; provenance vocabularies are standardised and should not be reinvented; and public-authority standards require publishing performance data. Exceptions need explicit modelling because degraded intake is where legal deadlines are most often breached.

layers.name: Exchange and Interoperability
layers.description: Packaging the request for transmission and binding it to external profiles without letting a serialisation become the semantics.

findings.name: Exchange packaging, profile binding and standards alignment
findings.description: The same request may need to appear as a filing message, a service-request resource, an evidence exchange payload or a domain exchange package. These are projections; the model must declare mappings and their loss characteristics rather than adopt any one as its structure.

questions.text: Which external profiles is this request expected to be expressed in, and which elements have no counterpart in each?
Is a mapping asserted as an alignment or claimed as conformance, and what evidence supports a conformance claim?
How are correlation identifiers preserved across an exchange so a response can be matched to the original request?
What happens when the receiving system's profile version differs from the sending system's?

data_elements.name: Profile binding
data_elements.description: Declared mapping from this model to an external exchange profile, with version and loss notes.

data_elements.name: Correlation and idempotency key
data_elements.description: Value used to match responses and to make retried submissions safe.

artifacts.name: Request exchange package
artifacts.description: A serialised, profile-conformant projection of the request assembled for transmission to a specific counterparty, retained alongside the semantic record as evidence of what was actually sent.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Request identifier plus counterparty identifier plus transmission sequence number; the exchange system's own message identifier takes precedence as the authoritative key when it issues one.

layers.name: Provenance, Measurement and Exception Handling
layers.description: Attributable history, published performance, and defensible behaviour under failure.

findings.name: Provenance and chain of custody
findings.description: Provenance answers who or what generated each version of the request, from what it was derived, and on whose behalf agents acted. Reusing a standard provenance vocabulary keeps this verifiable across organisational boundaries.

questions.text: Which activity generated each version of the request record, and which agent was associated with that activity?
From which prior entities was this request derived - a draft, a previous request, a pre-filled dataset?
Where a software agent acted, on whose authority did it act and how is that delegation recorded?
Which custody boundaries did the record cross, and was integrity verified at each crossing?

data_elements.name: Generation activity
data_elements.description: The activity that produced a version of the request, with agent, instants and inputs used.

data_elements.name: Derivation link
data_elements.description: Reference to an entity this request or version was derived from, with derivation type.

data_elements.name: Delegation record
data_elements.description: Assertion that one agent acted on behalf of another, with basis and validity.

artifacts.name: Provenance bundle
artifacts.description: A self-contained, attributable set of provenance assertions about the request, exportable so that a third party can reconstruct how the record came to be without access to the originating system.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Named by an IRI derived from the authoritative request identifier; the bundle itself is an entity with its own generation activity and attribution, so it must carry a distinct identifier from the request it describes.

findings.name: Intake performance measurement and published reporting
findings.description: Public-authority standards require defining what success looks like and publishing performance data. Measurement definitions must be recorded with the request-level facts that feed them, or published figures cannot be reproduced or audited.

questions.text: Which measures are computed over request records, and from exactly which recorded instants and codes?
How is timeliness measured against the statutory period, including suspended and extended cases?
Which measures are published, at what aggregation, and how is disclosure of small cohorts prevented from re-identifying requesters?
How are intake quality problems - rejection rate, deficiency rate, channel abandonment - fed back into the form and rules?

data_elements.name: Measure definition reference
data_elements.description: Pointer to the definition of a computed measure, including its source fields and formula.

data_elements.name: Elapsed processing time
data_elements.description: Duration from clock start to disposition, with suspensions excluded, computed from recorded instants.

data_elements.name: Deadline breach indicator
data_elements.description: Whether the applicable deadline was exceeded, with reason where it was.

artifacts.name: Published intake performance report
artifacts.description: The periodic, aggregated report of intake volumes, timeliness, rejection and deficiency rates published for the procedure, together with the measure definitions needed to reproduce it.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Procedure identifier plus reporting period expressed as an explicit RFC 3339 interval; the period, not the publication date, identifies the report.

findings.name: Exception handling, outages and erroneous submissions
findings.description: Intake fails in specific, foreseeable ways: the channel is unavailable at a deadline, a submission is duplicated by a retry, content is wrong, or an exchange partner is down. Each needs a defined, evidenced treatment because legal consequences attach.

questions.text: If the submission channel is unavailable at or near a deadline, what fallback exists and how is the outage evidenced?
answer_data: Outage record with start and end instants

questions.text: How are retried or duplicated submissions distinguished from genuine repeat requests?
How is a record that should never have existed marked and treated, and is it destroyed or retained annotated?
When an upstream evidence provider or exchange partner fails, what error is surfaced to the requester and what is the recovery path?
answer_data: Manual fallback and its clock effect

questions.text: How are partial submissions and abandoned drafts treated - are they records at all?
answer_data: Conversion event to a submitted request

data_elements.name: Exception record
data_elements.description: A captured failure affecting the request, with type, origin, instants, impact and resolution.

data_elements.name: Entered-in-error indicator
data_elements.description: Marks a record created in error, distinct from a properly cancelled or withdrawn request.

data_elements.name: Outage relief determination
data_elements.description: Whether a deadline was relieved because of a channel outage, with basis and authorising agent.

artifacts.name: Intake exception record
artifacts.description: The retained record of an outage, duplicate, erroneous entry or partner failure affecting one or more requests, including its impact on deadlines and the relief granted.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Exception register serial as the authoritative key, cross-referenced to every affected request identifier; the register is independent of the request so a single outage is recorded once.

functions.name: Submit request
functions.description: Perform the submission act: bind a payload to a procedure, attach evidence, capture the authentication context and create the request record in its initial state.
inputs: Declared payload conforming to the form definition
outputs: Request record in its initial state
Submission instant and ingestion instant recorded separately
preconditions: The procedure is open for submission at the submission instant
Any collection approval required for the form is current
Mandatory items are present or the channel permits staged completion
effects: Creates an immutable as-filed payload version
Assigns internal surrogate identity pending registration
Starts provenance with a generation activity attributed to the submitting agent

functions.name: Register request and acknowledge receipt
functions.description: Enter the request on the register, mint the authoritative identifier and issue the acknowledgement stating the processing period, redress routes and any tacit-approval effect.
inputs: Applicable processing period and legal basis
outputs: Tracking reference disclosed to the requester
preconditions: Receipt instant has been captured
The receiving body accepts the request as within its intake scope, or records that it does not
effects: Fixes the clock-start instant
Makes the request externally addressable for status query
Creates the receipt artefact as evidence that the acknowledgement duty was met

functions.name: Validate technical conformance
functions.description: Run structural, code-list, cross-field and cross-record validation against the pinned rule-set version and emit a citable issue list.
outputs: Issue list with codes and element locations
preconditions: The form definition version is resolvable
Referenced code systems are available or a cached snapshot is declared
effects: Records the rule-set version used so the result stays reproducible
May place the request in a blocked technical state without affecting legal admissibility

functions.name: Screen completeness and determine admissibility
functions.description: Assess whether every mandatory requirement is discharged, issue a deficiency notice where it is not, and record the effect on the processing clock.
inputs: Requirement set from the procedure catalogue
preconditions: Registration has occurred
The requirement set version applicable at submission is resolvable
effects: May suspend the clock on a stated legal basis
Sets the effective submission instant where it differs from first receipt
Starts the cure period

functions.name: Retrieve evidence from an authoritative source
functions.description: On the requester's explicit request, obtain evidence from the competent providing authority, offer preview where required and bind the result to the requirement it discharges.
preconditions: An explicit request by the user exists and is in scope
The requirement is mapped to an available evidence type at the providing authority
effects: Adds evidence without asking the applicant again
Records the retrieval as a provenance activity with both authorities as agents
On preview rejection, leaves the requirement undischarged and notifies the requester

functions.name: Amend, supplement or withdraw the request
functions.description: Apply a permitted change class, creating a new version linked by derivation and recomputing any affected dates without erasing prior state.
outputs: Recomputed effective submission instant and deadline
preconditions: The change class is permitted in the current state
The acting party holds authority to make the change
effects: Prior version remains immutable and retrievable
May trigger re-screening and revalidation
On withdrawal, sets a terminal disposition and determines refund entitlement

functions.name: Determine competence, transfer and assign a processing track
functions.description: Identify the competent body and component, transfer where necessary preserving the original receipt date, and place the request in a processing track.
preconditions: The request is registered
Competence rules for the procedure are resolvable
effects: Carries the original receipt instant forward across transfer
Constrains the maximum internal transfer window used in clock computation
Makes queue ordering auditable

functions.name: Compute and manage processing time limits
functions.description: Derive the deadline from recorded instants and the applicable period, apply suspensions and extensions with notice, and evaluate any expiry consequence.
inputs: Applicable period, calendar basis and legal basis
outputs: Extension grant with justification and notice
preconditions: The clock-start instant is fixed and recorded with an explicit offset
The period is published in advance
effects: Deadline is always recomputable from the event history rather than stored as an unexplained value
Notice is dispatched before expiry where an extension is taken
Records a deemed outcome where silence has legal effect

functions.name: Dispose the request by opening a case, fulfilling or refusing
functions.description: End the request's own lifecycle by linking a case, recording direct fulfilment, or issuing a reasoned refusal with redress information.
inputs: Case identifier where a case is opened
Reasons and legal basis where adverse
outputs: Reasoned determination and redress notice artefact
preconditions: Admissibility has been determined
Where adverse, the requester has had any applicable opportunity to be heard
effects: Transfers substantive handling to the neighbouring case model
Starts the redress clock from the notification instant
Typically starts the retention clock for the request record

functions.name: Export a profile-conformant exchange package
functions.description: Project the request into a declared external profile for transmission, preserving correlation identifiers, access markings and integrity values.
preconditions: A declared mapping to the target profile exists
The requester or legal basis permits disclosure to the counterparty
effects: Records exactly what was sent, to whom and when
Carries access markings and recipient obligations with the package
Does not alter the semantic record, which remains format-neutral

functions.name: Apply retention rule and execute disposition
functions.description: Bind the request to its retention rule via classification, detect the retention trigger, honour any legal hold and execute the due disposal action with evidence.
preconditions: A disposition authority covering this record class is in force
No unreleased legal hold applies to the scope
effects: Destroys, transfers or permanently retains content per the authorised action
Preserves disposal evidence after the content is gone
Applies variant rules to withdrawn, refused and erroneous requests where authorised

functions.name: Mark a record entered in error and retract downstream
functions.description: Distinguish a record that should never have existed from a properly cancelled one, annotate it, and notify downstream consumers of the retraction.
preconditions: An authorised agent has determined the record is erroneous
Downstream consumers of the record are identifiable from the exchange history
effects: Preserves the original for audit rather than deleting it, unless disposal is separately authorised
Excludes the record from performance measures with the exclusion recorded
Prevents silent divergence between the master record and previously exported copies

composition.purpose: Specialise the generic record model for the request case. Record characteristics, base metadata and the record/agent/business/mandate/relationship entity view are inherited, not restated here.

Record the handover: the case identifier created when the request is admitted, and the typed relation between request and proceeding. The registry records WM-POL-017 as composing this model; from the request side the case is a forward reference, and it is optional because a request may be fulfilled or refused without opening a case.

composition.target: Public service / procedure catalogue model (CPSV-AP aligned)
composition.purpose: Resolve the procedure, its Requirements, Evidence types, Channels, Costs, Rules and Outputs. This model instantiates catalogue definitions and must cite the catalogue version rather than copy the definitions.

composition.target: Party / agent model (natural person and organisation)
composition.purpose: Resolve submitter, subject, representative, payer and notified-party references to governed party identities without embedding master data in the request.

Attach and reference evidence items whose content model, format and preservation are governed elsewhere; this model contributes the requirement-discharge link, sufficiency judgement and integrity values.

composition.target: Identity and trust-service model (authentication and assurance)
composition.purpose: Supply the authentication context and assurance level observed at the submission act, and validate signatures and seals against trust anchors, without duplicating credential lifecycle management.
Provide Entity/Activity/Agent, generation, derivation, attribution, association and delegation terms for the event history and provenance bundle rather than defining a bespoke audit vocabulary.

composition.target: Retention schedule and disposition authority model
composition.purpose: Inherit the retention rule from a classification under a named disposition authority, and record holds and executed disposal actions against that authority.
Link the fee assessment and its admissibility effect to the payment transaction, whose execution, settlement and refund mechanics are out of scope here.
Point to the grant, refusal, permit or award produced, which carries its own identity, effective dates and appeal window.
